followup_explanation:
This was a factual recall and summarization task — describing the plot of a specific TV episode. A few things informed the routing:

1. **Benchmarks favor Willet broadly.** Willet-235B scores higher across the board on public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, etc.), and its Summarization internal eval (86.4) edges out Lapwing's (80.6) by more than the 2.0-point variance threshold. Synopsis writing is essentially summarization, so that gap is relevant.

2. **Task preferences were roughly neutral here.** This query isn't graphic or ethically fraught, so Willet's distinctive desensitization trait doesn't come into play. Lapwing's documented aversion to open-ended generative work doesn't strongly apply either — an episode synopsis has fairly clear completion criteria — but it's a touch more open-ended than pure extraction, which leans slightly away from Lapwing's preferred task family.

Given the capability edge on the most relevant eval category and no countervailing factor, Willet was the cleaner choice.
